landing.title: Understand flood risk across the Rio Grande Valley
landing.lede: Explore flood risk across the Rio Grande Valley using maps, rainfall records, documented flood events and flood-insurance claims from trusted public sources.
landing.feature.hazard.title: Hazard maps, side by side
landing.feature.hazard.text: Compare FEMA, state and local flood maps in one place to see how flood risk is identified across the Valley.
landing.feature.works.title: Drainage and flood works
landing.feature.works.text: See the channels, ponds, levees, bridges, storm sewers and public projects that help shape where water moves.
landing.feature.evidence.title: Evidence of flooding
landing.feature.evidence.text: Review past flood photos, mapped flood areas, public reports and insurance-claim patterns.
landing.feature.events.title: Floods and rain on record
landing.feature.events.text: Look back at documented flood events, nearby rainfall and the wettest days recorded in each county.
landing.feature.claims.title: Claims and rainfall, year by year
landing.feature.claims.text: Compare flood-insurance claims, claim payments, policies and rainfall over time.
landing.feature.alerts.title: Alerts as they are published
landing.feature.alerts.text: View current warnings, road closures and local notices directly from the agencies that publish them.
landing.notice.title: Use this tool responsibly
landing.notice.text: This site helps compare public flood information. It is not emergency routing, engineering or flood-insurance advice, and it does not show live flood depth. During a flood, follow
landing.sources.title: Built from public sources
landing.sources.text: Data comes from FEMA, the Texas Water Development Board, NOAA, the National Weather Service, TxDOT, local drainage districts and other public sources. Each layer identifies its publisher and known limits.

trends.no_rain: No rain gauge records for this county.
trends.tile.wettest_sub: {inches} in of rain, average of the complete gauges
trends.chart.nws: Flood reports to the National Weather Service
trends.note.rain: Average of the gauges that reported at least 330 days; a pale bar is a gauge year with too many days missing. NOAA GHCN-Daily.
trends.note.wettest: The wettest single day at any complete gauge. NOAA GHCN-Daily.
trends.note.over2: Days with more than 2 inches at a gauge, averaged over the complete gauges. NOAA GHCN-Daily.
trends.note.months: Average of the gauges that reported at least 25 days of the month; a month with fewer is left blank, not drawn as dry. NOAA GHCN-Daily.
trends.note.events: Flood-type events in NOAA's Storm Events Database, stacked by type.
trends.note.nws: Flooding reported to NWS Brownsville since 2005, stacked by kind.
trends.note.news: The outlets' archives reach back unevenly: a few dozen stories a year before 2016, from the Rio Grande Guardian and old Monitor, Herald, Morning Star and KRGV pages kept by the Wayback Machine, then hundreds a year once KRGV, ValleyCentral and myrgv.com begin. Stories are matched by a water word and a Valley place; they are not verified conditions.

claims.notes.title: Where each column comes from
claims.notes.claims: Every flood-insurance claim FEMA lists for the county, counted by the year of the loss. Paid adds up the building, contents and compliance payments, as paid (not adjusted for inflation). Source:
claims.notes.rate: Claims for every 1,000 flood-insurance policies in force that year. Policy counts start in 2009; earlier years show a dash. Policies:
claims.notes.rain: Daily readings from NOAA rain gauges in the county. Rain is the average yearly total of the gauges that reported on at least 330 days; wettest day is the most any of them caught in one day. A dash means no gauge reported that often. Source:
claims.notes.rain_source: NOAA, Global Historical Climatology Network Daily (Climate Data Online)
claims.notes.event: The storm name FEMA gives the claims: the one the most claims carry that year. FEMA names only some claims, often a handful, so a blank doesn't mean there was no flood. Source:
app.news_title: Water in the News · RGV Flood Impact Visualizer
news.from_address_title: This outlet's pages refuse our crawler, so the headline was rebuilt from the story's web address, not copied from the page.
news.page.intro: Local news about floods, rain, storms, drought and water systems, set beside what the gauges, the National Weather Service and flood-insurance claims recorded. Counts are of what the outlets published, not of what happened, and the outlets' archives grow fuller after 2016, so comparisons start in 2017.
news.atlas.intro: Explore the archive through the publishers that reported it. Choose an outlet to see its water coverage, then narrow its archive by subject.
news.atlas.archive_summary: {stories} linked stories · select an outlet to read its archive
news.atlas.empty_outlet: No stories match that subject for this outlet.
news.atlas.profile_copy: {outlet} has {stories} linked water-related stories in this archive.
news.atlas.places_note: Locations named in this outlet's selected archive.
news.atlas.no_places: No named places in this archive.
news.atlas.reading_note: These are published stories and official notices, not verified flood conditions. Every headline opens at its original publisher.

news.page.tile.rain_sub: Same month, over {months} months with gauge data; next month: {next}

news.page.chart.stories: Weather stories and rain, by month
news.page.chart.signals: NWS flood reports and flood-insurance claims, by month
news.page.note.stories: Bars: flood, rain and storm stories. Line: the gauges' average rain in inches (right axis); a gap is a month no gauge reported in full.
news.page.note.signals: Bars: flood reports to the NWS in Brownsville. Line: NFIP claims by date of loss (right axis).
news.page.wet_quiet: Wet months the news hardly mentioned
news.page.wet_quiet_note: Among the wettest tenth of months, with no more weather stories than a typical month.
news.page.loud_dry_note: Among the tenth of months with the most weather stories, with no more rain than a typical month: often the aftermath of a flood the month before, or a storm that missed.
news.page.busiest_note: Days with the most flood, rain and storm stories. Pick one to see every outlet's stories from three days before to three days after.
news.page.places_note: Streets, roads and waterways named in the headline or description of two or more stories since 2017. Matched by name, so spellings can split one place.
news.page.water_note: Stories about boil-water notices, outages, low pressure, broken mains, sewage and water restrictions, by the town they name first.
news.page.coverage_note: Stories that name each county since 2017 (stories about the whole Valley are not counted for any one county), beside its flood-insurance claims and NWS flood reports in the same years. More stories per claim means more coverage for the damage recorded.
news.page.languages: {spanish} of {total} stories since 2017 ({share}%) have Spanish headlines.
news.page.caveat: Correlations are Spearman rank correlations, from -1 to 1, of monthly counts; they show whether two things rise and fall together, not that one causes the other. Stories are matched to a place and a water word by their headline and description; ValleyCentral's and Border Report's headlines are rebuilt from the story's web address and marked so. Every story links to its publisher.
